**Answer: 6**

The student cannot tell which floor any button corresponds to, and the example says a single lit button always looks the same. So the observation cannot depend on which buttons are lit, only on how many are lit. Any permutation of the six buttons must leave the observation unchanged.

Under that reading, two lit-button sets give the same observation exactly when they have the same size. The sizes that are possible, given at least one button is lit, are 1 through 6, so there are 6 distinct observations.

ANSWER: 6
